title: AI Use and Verification
text:
Substantive prompts

I am creating a regression case study in R and Quarto. My question is “What are the most relevant factors for predicting a customer’s annual health insurance charges?”. The response is charges (continuous numeric variable), the main predictors are age, sex, bmi, children, smoker, and region, and my course-based core model is lm(charges ~ age + sex + bmi + children + smoker + region, data = health_insurance). My main result so far is: Residual standard error: 6062 on 1329 degrees of freedom; Multiple R-squared: 0.7509; Adjusted R-squared: 0.7494; F-statistic: 500.8 on 8 and 1329 DF; p-value: < 2.2e-16. I found this limitation or opportunity: One opportunity for improvement is to incorporate the slight differences in interactions between smoker status and gender into the model. Suggest three feasible extensions that keep the core analysis connected to regression methods taught in my class. One option may be a model not taught in class used as a comparator. For each, explain how it strengthens the same research question, how its result would enter the final case study, the implementation steps, and two ways I could verify it. Do not choose for me.

title: AI Use and Verification
text:
My decisions

Accepted: It suggested we use a random forest to capture nonlinear patterns and interactions that the baseline formula may miss. It also suggested incorporating interactions into the model.
Changed: Of the suggestions listed above, no changes needed to be made to the extension or its verifications.
Rejected or corrected: It wanted to square the age and bmi predictors which may not be necessary, or atleast more research would have to be done before assuming that it is.
